knowledgeAnswers.rationale: High-visibility clothing, gloves and any other PPE the site requires are the minimum for litter picking beside vehicles. Sunglasses, a hard hat alone, or no extra PPE do not meet the procedure.
The worker marks the sharp, keeps others away, and calls a trained colleague with a sharps container. Handling it by hand or leaving it unmarked is not permitted.
Sharps go into a rigid sharps container, never into a sack or general waste.
The equipment and personal protection section says to wear the gloves issued to you at all times while picking.

practicalCriteria: Learner sets up barriers and signs around a supplied external area, with high-visibility clothing and gloves on, before picking up any litter.
Learner handles a supplied mock sharp using a litter picker and places it into a rigid container, or marks it and calls for a trained colleague, without touching it by hand.
Learner sorts general litter into a sack and sharps into a rigid container, keeping the two separate.
Learner replaces a supplied protective screen or cage to its original condition, and empties and returns a bin to its original position.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Job sheet with the boundary confirmed by the site contact
Assessor observation of the barrier set-up and sharps handling
Record of any item found, its location and the action taken
stopWorkCriteria: Boundary of the work area is unclear or not agreed
Sharp is in a place that cannot be reached safely
A vehicle or member of the public enters the work area
Worker is not wearing high-visibility clothing or gloves
